CVE-2026-119446.title: Session fixation in the CLI login flow allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain a user's API token
CVE-2026-119446.description:
Session Fixation vulnerability in the CLI login flow in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an unauthenticated attacker to obtain an API token for another user's account via a crafted login link. Starting a CLI login with POST /api/auth/cli_session needs no authentication and returns a polling token, a confirmation URL that carries that token, and a confirmation code. When a signed-in user opens that URL and clicks Confirm, NervesHub.Accounts.verify_cli_session_token/2 creates an API token for the user's account and stores it on the login, and the next poll of GET /api/auth/cli_session/<token> returns it to whoever started the login.

The confirmation code is only displayed and is never compared with anything, so it cannot show that the person confirming is the one who started the login. The confirm form carries a CSRF token and the page cannot be framed, so the attacker has to persuade the user to open the link and click the button themselves.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 2.5.0…

CVE-2026-129984.title: AutoGPT: Billing managers are treated as ordinary members and can read teammates' runs
CVE-2026-129984.description: AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.67 to 0.11.2, organization and team billing-manager roles intended only for spend management are treated as ordinary members across workflow, run, library, and marketplace routes. Although the role matrix in autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/permissions.py withholds run access and workflow creation, those routes do not enforce the matrix and their underlying membership lookups ignore the caller's role. As a result, a team billing manager can read team workflows and other members' runs (including inputs, outputs, and per-node data), while an organization billing manager can view shared workflows and runs and create workflows and marketplace listings; neither can modify or delete other members' workflows. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.3.

CVE-2026-135390.title: Pion DTLS: Client authentication bypass when client and server connections share a session store
CVE-2026-135390.description: Pion DTLS is a Go implementation of Datagram Transport Layer Security. From 2.1.0 until 3.1.14, a listener performing DTLS 1.2 resumption accepted a session created by an outbound client connection without checking which role created it. A malicious server previously contacted by the application can retain the outbound session secret, select the client-side cached session through its session key, and present it to the application's reachable listener when both connections share a SessionStore. The attacker must first complete an outbound connection. WebRTC users are not affected. The listener can accept application data without running its normal PSK callback or client-certificate authentication checks, allowing a peer trusted only for an outbound connection to gain unauthorized listener access. The issue is fixed in version 3.1.14.

CVE-2026-41327.title: Dgraph: Pre-Auth Full Database Exfiltration via DQL Injection in Upsert Condition Field
CVE-2026-41327.description: Dgraph is an open source distributed GraphQL database. Prior to 25.3.3, a vulnerability has been found in Dgraph that gives an unauthenticated attacker full read access to every piece of data in the database. This affects Dgraph's default configuration where ACL is not enabled. The attack is a single HTTP POST to /mutate?commitNow=true containing a crafted cond field in an upsert mutation. The cond value is concatenated directly into a DQL query string via strings.Builder.WriteString after only a cosmetic strings.Replace transformation. No escaping, parameterization, or structural validation is applied. An attacker injects an additional DQL query block into the cond string, which the DQL parser accepts as a syntactically valid named query block. The injected query executes server-side and its results are returned in the HTTP response. This vulnerability is fixed in 25.3.3.

CVE-2026-92697.title: FastNetMon: NetFlow v9 unbounded strlen() on interface-description field causes remote out-of-bounds read
CVE-2026-92697.description: FastNetMon is a high-performance DDoS detector and sensor. In version 1.2.9 and earlier, the NetFlow v9 collector calls strlen() on an attacker-controlled interface-description field without bounding the scan to the field’s declared length. An unauthenticated remote attacker who can send crafted UDP packets to the collector can trigger an out-of-bounds read and potentially crash the process, causing denial of service. No fixed release is available as of this review.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

NFSv4/flexfiles: fail I/O to the data server once a lock is lost

When a client loses a byte-range lock, because its lease expired and it
may not recover the lock (nfs.recover_lost_locks=0) or because reclaim
failed, it marks the lock state NFS_LOCK_LOST and fails further I/O by
that lock owner. Otherwise an application that believes it holds a
lock over a range is never told that the lock is gone, and can
overwrite data that another client has since written under its own
lock on that range.

The NFSv4 READ/WRITE and file layout I/O paths apply this in
rpc_call_prepare, where nfs4_set_rw_stateid() returns -EIO for a lost
lock. The flexfiles data server I/O path does not: the NFSv3 data
server path never checked, and the check on the NFSv4 path was removed
when the data server stateid began to be taken from the layout.
